title: Collection from Wastewater Treatment Plant, Transportation, and Storage of Raw Wastewater
author: Kevin Calci
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bycepste

steps.title: Coordinate sampling with facility
steps.instruction: Discuss sampling requirements with WWTP management before starting, especially if using the plant’s automated sampler, which is generally not set up for aseptic sampling.

steps.title: Prepare containers and labeling
steps.instruction: Use new sample containers; if unavailable, clean and autoclave‑sterilize them. Label each container with an indelible marker or waterproof label.

steps.title: Program and calibrate ISCO sampler
steps.instruction: Follow the manufacturer’s instructions to program the ISCO for flow‑paced or time‑paced composite sampling and to calibrate its collection volume so that 3–4 cm headspace remains in each bottle; calibration need not be repeated at every occasion.

steps.title: Position ISCO suction line
steps.instruction: Place the ISCO suction line downstream of the headworks, preferably after the screener and de‑gritting, and set the weighted suction strainer in a zone of high hydraulic turbulence without touching the channel bottom or sides.

steps.title: Ensure container headspace
steps.instruction: Verify that each sample bottle contains at least 3–4 cm of empty space to allow complete mixing before analysis.

steps.title: Collect sample with peristaltic pump
steps.instruction: Insert the pump suction line into the designated collection area, start the pump, purge tubing by directing the outlet flow into the influent stream until roughly 1 L has flushed the line, stop the pump, move the outlet to the labeled container, run the pump to deliver the intended volume, stop, cap tightly, then run the pump in reverse to empty remaining tubing.

steps.title: Collect sample with dip pole
steps.instruction: Secure a clean collection bottle on the dip pole, dip it into the designated area and rinse at least three times with influent flow, collect the sample, transfer the wastewater into the pre‑labeled container (do not collect directly in the container), and cap.

steps.title: Cool samples during collection
steps.instruction: Fill the ISCO base with ice, secure bottles in proper orientation, add ice around them to keep samples cool, and, if available, place a temperature‑recording device (e.g., Smart Button) with each bottle.

steps.title: Retrieve and handle overfilled bottles
steps.instruction: After the programmed collection period, return to the WWTP, retrieve the filled bottles; if any bottle is overfilled, do not pour out sample but transfer the contents to a larger vessel for adequate mixing at the laboratory, and recalibrate the ISCO for the next run.

steps.title: Package samples for transport
steps.instruction: Place each bottle in a polyethylene secondary‑containment bag, then set the bags on wet ice inside an insulated cooler; use a rack to keep bottles upright when possible.

steps.title: Seal and disinfect bottle exteriors
steps.instruction: Tightly seal each bottle and decontaminate its outer surface with a bleach‑based disinfectant such as Hype‑Wipes.

steps.title: Maintain transport temperature
steps.instruction: Ensure sufficient ice is present to keep sample temperature below 8 °C for the entire transport; if shipping commercially, comply with IATA regulations for biological substances.

steps.title: Store samples before analysis
steps.instruction: If analysis cannot occur within 7 days, store samples at 2–8 °C; for storage longer than 7 days, freeze at –20 °C or –70 °C.
